Under the modern majority rule, the niece has no interest. "To cousin and the heirs of his body" would have created a fee tail at common law, but most states have abolished the fee tail and convert it into a fee simple absolute in the cousin. The grantor therefore kept no reversion, so his later deed to the niece passed nothing. (A minority of states that instead give the cousin a life estate with a remainder to his heirs would leave the niece only a reversion.)

CONFIDENCE: 80
